source: National Archives Constitution transcript, Article III Section 3
review_notes: Codex reviewed the complete section. The two definitions of treason are alternatives; adhering to enemies requires giving aid and comfort. The conviction rule preserves the two-witness overt-act and open-court confession alternatives without asserting that either alone guarantees conviction. The forfeiture limit applies beyond the attainted person’s life. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
Article. III.
Section. 3.
Treason against the United States, shall consist only in levying War against them, or in adhering to their Enemies, giving them Aid and Comfort. No Person shall be convicted of Treason unless on the Testimony of two Witnesses to the same overt Act, or on Confession in open Court.
The Congress shall have Power to declare the Punishment of Treason, but no Attainder of Treason shall work Corruption of Blood, or Forfeiture except during the Life of the Person attainted.
